scope: Same ordinary element, document timeline, fixed registration and numeric values; no scroll timelines, dynamic registration, inheritance, pseudo-elements, attr/URL inputs, transitions or iterations beyond first.
shared_protocol: Use fresh target and distinct registered names per case; assert typed registration on independent ordinary calibration target.
Use explicit duration1000, linear easing, fillboth; pause all effects and set currentTime before samples. Keep provider and consumer objects separately identified.

Save first consumer scalar before provider getters or a forced normal recascade; then record provider values, repeated reads, currentTime/playState and authored getKeyframes. Timing calibration failure makes the result inconclusive.
Retain both creation orders where specified; no expected failure count. Cancel animations and remove only owned targets in test cleanup.
Reuse existing ordinary typed-cycle/defaulting controls and neutral registered/additive crash tests; do not claim numeric cycle semantics from a no-crash result.

cases.setup: Registered numbers p/q, non-inherited initial 2/3. Base p=7. Lower p endpoints10/30 replace, higher p endpoints4/8 add; consumer q has identical var(p) replace endpoints. All1000ms at500ms.
cases.variants: Create q before both p effects, between them, and after both; preserve p composite order.
cases.distinguishes: Full provider stack versus creation-order partial map or old base7.

cases.setup: Same p stack (26). q base99, lower q constant20 replace, upper q has only offset1 var(p), replace, at500ms of1000ms.
cases.distinguishes: Implicit zero endpoint is lower q prefix20, not base99 or final q; authored endpoint reads full current p26.

cases.setup: p=13!important; p animation has identical var(q) endpoints, q animation identical var(p) endpoints; registered p/q non-inherited numbers.
cases.distinguishes: Do not create a final-provider cycle from a masked p animation. Both individual endpoint computations can still be well-defined.

cases.setup: p animation identical13 endpoints; q animation identical var(p,var(q)) endpoints, distinct registered numbers.
cases.distinguishes: Actual var fallback demand, not union of syntactic references.

cases.setup: p lower constant10; p higher constant50 replace; q identical var(p) endpoints.
cases.distinguishes: Highest contributing provider and numeric prefix pruning. Does not establish cycle-pruning equivalence.

cases.setup: p number initial10, base50; single add animation with identical var(p,91) endpoints, at500ms.
cases.record: p, ordinary downstream width calc(var(p)*1px), repeated reads, playState/currentTime. No hypothesis becomes a PASS oracle.

cases.setup: x/y number initials10/20 bases77/88; x endpoints var(y,91)/100; y endpoints200/var(x,92); both500ms. Reverse creation order on independent target.
cases.record: x/y first and repeated samples, downstream consumers and per-animation timing. Preserve every result.

cases.setup: q number initial7/base99; q keyframes offset0=10,offset.5=20,offset1=var(q,91); sample250ms of1000ms then750ms, independent reversed-observation target.
cases.record: Tests computed-keyframe-before-selection boundary; 15 is not asserted as normative in the cyclic setup.

cases.setup: p lower identical var(q), p higher identical50 replace, q identical var(p); numbers initial10/20. Lower p numeric contribution discarded.
cases.record: Whether lower endpoint evaluation changes cycle state cannot be inferred solely from arithmetic pruning. Compare with literal-complete-replacement and retain authored keyframes.
